chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Sama'ah who said:
"Whoever recites 'Iqra' bi-ismi rabbika' (Read in the name of your Lord), when he finishes it, let him prostrate; and when he stands up, let him recite Al-Fatihah and bow."

He said, "And if you are tested with it (this method) alongside an Imam who does not prostrate, then nodding and bowing will suffice for you; and do not recite 'Iqra' in the obligatory prayer, recite it in the voluntary prayer."

key_terms.اَلْإِيمَاءُ: Nodding (a gesture of assent or acknowledgment, often used for prostration or bowing when standing is difficult)
key_terms.اِقْرَأْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ: Read in the name of your Lord (referring to Surah Al-Ikhlas or a short surah)

ai.seo_question: How should one pray if the Imam does not prostrate after reciting a short surah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the practice of *Sajdat al-Tilawah* (prostration of recitation) following the recitation of Surah Al-Ikhlas, a practice emphasized in Shia jurisprudence. It provides a practical ruling for congregational prayer: if the Imam does not perform this prostration, the follower may indicate it through nodding (*i'ma'*) and bowing, while reserving the full recitation of the short surah for voluntary (*Tawattu'*) prayers to avoid confusion or deviation from the Imam's action.
